newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index closes at record high.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index closes at record high.

text.p: * Value turnover remains heavy at 4.3 billion pesos
The Manila composite share index ended at an all-time high of 3,447.60 points on Monday, the third consecutive session that the market closed at a record, traders said.

"It looks like the fundamentals are just too good to be overlooked so that even if we were in negative territory in the early part of the session, there was follow-up buying," said Lito Vicencio, sales head at Peregrine Securities Inc.
The main index rose 25.69 points, or 0.75 percent, from the previous close of 3,421.91. Gainers trounced losers, 89 to 46 with 71 issues unchanged.

Traders were earlier expecting the market to correct due to its runup last week. Increased cash needs for the Chinese New Year as well as the fall in New York last Friday of the Dow and PLDT's ADR might also have triggered selling, they said.
Of the firstliners, Meralco, Metrobank, Ayala Land B and First Philippine Holdings Corp B helped pull the index up.
Last week, the main index reached record closing highs on Thursday and Friday.
Earlier in the week, it had notched an intra-day record.
The recent run-up, said to be triggered by strong corporate earnings and a good economic situation, has shaken the market out of its downtrend in the last quarter of 1996.
The previous record high of the index was at 3,375.94 reached in July, 1996.

"We could still expect some temporary weakness but it's nothing to be alarmed about and it might even be an opportunity for others who missed last week's rally to get in. These prices are not ridiculous and we are nowhere near that irrational exuberance," Nathan Lozada, assistant vice-president at Philippine Asia Equity, said.
